quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the tire locked until you stop.
Keep squeezing the front brake lever.
Release the front brake and apply it again right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake and apply it again right away.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake pressure. Then apply the brake again with steady, controlled pressure.

questions.question: When making a normal stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use both the front and rear brakes at the same time and downshift.

questions.question: Should you wear hearing protection when riding?

options.text: No, it is not recommended.
Yes, only on long rides.
Yes, on every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, on every ride.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet on. Wear hearing protection every time you ride to protect your hearing.

questions.question: How should you use the front brake?

options.text: Use it only in emergencies.
Use it with the rear brake.
Do not use it—it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use it with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go slowly and be careful.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, stop completely and wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing. Never try to go around a train.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Go through the intersection carefully.
Yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Stop completely and wait for a signal that lets you turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT true about a motorcycle that fits a rider?

options.text: The rider's feet can touch the ground while sitting.
The controls are easy to reach and use.
The handlebars are above the rider's head while sitting.

questions.correctAnswerText: The handlebars are above the rider's head while sitting.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits a rider if the feet touch the ground while sitting and the controls are easy to reach. Riding a motorcycle that does not fit is unsafe.

questions.question: Why do motorcycles have an advantage over cars when passing parked vehicles?

options.text: Motorcycles can speed up faster than cars.
The rider can move to the left side of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
Motorcycles can stop shorter than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider can move to the left side of the lane to avoid doors and people on the right.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars on your right, ride on the left side of your lane. This helps you avoid opening doors, people getting out, or people stepping between vehicles. Only do this if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to ride safely:

options.text: Gets better.
Stays the same.
Gets worse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gets worse.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride your motorcycle if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: It affects your steering and balance.
It stops the front brake from working.
It prevents you from going faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It affects your steering and balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it makes steering harder, which affects your balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: A motorized scooter can:

options.text: Only be operated during the day.
Be operated without a driver license.
Be operated with any class of driver license.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be operated with any class of driver license.
questions.explanation: In California, you can operate a motorized scooter with any class of driver license.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit with your posture allowing your arms to control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be used to hold up your body or support your weight.

questions.question: One problem with a motorcyclist riding directly next to another vehicle is that:

options.text: The other vehicle may block the motorcyclist's escape route.
The motorcyclist can be easily seen by other drivers.
The motorcyclist may not be able to read signs on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The other vehicle may block the motorcyclist's escape route.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The vehicle could swerve into your lane and hit you. It could also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection on every ride.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
Only stop to yield to other traffic.
Vehicles will be entering the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to all crossing traffic and pedestrians, then go when safe.

questions.question: You have a better chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear:

options.text: Face or eye protection.
A baseball cap.
Sneakers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield helps protect your face during a crash.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than you normally would.
Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller gaps of traffic than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This makes it respond more slowly to your movements. You need more time to slow down and stop. Start braking earlier, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Is very quickly absorbed into the bloodstream.
Needs to be digested to enter the bloodstream.
Can improve your riding ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very quickly absorbed into the bloodstream.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It goes directly into the bloodstream through the stomach and small intestine, reaching the brain quickly.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same location as they are on your motorcycle.
Immediately take it out on the highway.
Get familiar with it in a controlled area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a controlled area.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before riding a new motorcycle, find where all the controls are. Practice in a safe area before riding on the road.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Only ride in the left portion of the lane to better see around other vehicles ahead.
Ride closely to the vehicle in front of you to most effectively use their headlights.
Reduce your speed to increase your chances of avoiding an unexpected hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed to increase your chances of avoiding an unexpected hazard.
questions.explanation: At night, ride slower than during the day. This gives you more time to avoid hazards. Also increase your distance from other vehicles and adjust your position in the lane as needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Wear half-fingered gloves.
Wear full-fingered gloves.
Not wear gloves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear full-fingered gloves.
questions.explanation: Full-fingered gloves give you a better grip and protect your hands. Choose gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Ride within the posted speed limits.
Exceed the posted speed limit to complete the pass, but not by more than 10 mph.
Pass more than one vehicle at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride within the posted speed limits.
questions.explanation: You must stay within the speed limit when passing. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:

options.text: Leather.
Wool.
Any soft material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Leather or similar durable material gives the best grip and protection for riding gloves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.
